caption: LAUNCHED: the 12b duper with its stone swapped for a slime chain that carries a slime over the TNT cell during the push: every fresh TNT is flung north at exactly vz = -1.0 and vy = 0.1568 blocks/gt (only the cross axis keeps the random 0.02 kick); the judge measures the launch motion of every TNT

DROPPED straight down: the launching duper plus one stone as a north wall: every TNT is flung north, stops against the wall (its north-south position and motion exact) and falls straight down (horizontal motion under 0.01 blocks/gt at fuse 1), 72+ blocks by fuse 1

lever on/off AND survivable: the lever 12b with the launcher of tnt-launch-15b (its stone swapped for a slime chain carrying a slime over the TNT cell): every TNT is flung away at 1 block/gt and goes off out of range, so its explosions never reach the machine; runs while the input is off

PRECISE and SURVIVABLE: the precise water-channel aligner (a slime flings every TNT north at exactly 1 block/gt into a wall, the water current pins it at one point) on a SLOW engine: a 7-block crafter-loop clock (period 91 gt) holds the sticky piston out and releases it for 6 gt (the hold extended by a 4 gt repeater loop) so the 12b engine pushes once per period; one TNT alive at a time (91 gt > its 80 gt fuse), so no blast knocks the next one, and each goes off in the water (no block damage): every TNT at one point at fuse 1, bit for bit

TRIGGERED and SURVIVABLE: the lever engine (the 12b held still by power on its sticky piston) with the launcher of tnt-launch-15b, held by a redstone torch that the input pulse turns off through a dust and a stone: each pulse releases the piston for one push, one TNT flung away at 1 block/gt that goes off out of range
